attrs.management_says: Revenue growth led by Columbia brand (US, Canada), prAna brand ($56M incremental for first five months of 2015), and Sorel brand, with footwear up 19% and apparel up 9%.
attrs.numbers_show: Revenue rose 10.7% ($225.6M). Quarterly signals show H1 growth (+12.9% Q1, +17.3% Q2) consistent with prAna inclusion; H2 growth (+13.7% Q3, +3.3% Q4) reflects organic demand. Segment data reported in MD&A corroborates brand/region drivers.
attrs.verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers

attrs.management_says: Revenue growth led by Columbia brand, prAna acquisition (~$56M incremental for first five months of 2015), Sorel brand, and favorable channel mix shift to direct-to-consumer (E36, E37, E38).
attrs.numbers_show: Revenue grew 10.7% ($225.6M) to $2,326.2M. prAna incremental $56M accounts for ~25% of growth. Gross margin expanded to 46.1% from 45.5%, consistent with higher DTC mix (E12, E23, E37). Quarterly growth strong in Q1-Q3 (+12.9% to +17.3%) but slowed to +3.3% in Q4 (E25-E28).

attrs.management_says: Gross margin expansion driven by favorable channel mix (higher DTC, lower international distributor sales) (E38).
attrs.numbers_show: Gross margin improved 45.5%→46.1% (implied from E37). The shift to DTC (higher margin, faster cash collection) and away from distributors (lower margin, longer terms) is consistent with stable/improving annual DSO despite Q3/Q4 deterioration.

attrs.reason: Quarterly revenue signals (E25-E28) show H1 growth higher, consistent with prAna acquisition timing; MD&A segment breakdown (E35-E37) reports brand-level contributions including $56M prAna incremental, which together with total revenue growth (E12, E33) corroborate the stated drivers at the right magnitude.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The revenue growth drivers cited by management are corroborated by the reported revenue increase of 10.7% (E12, E33) and the segment breakdowns in MD&A (E35-E37) showing Columbia, prAna ($56M incremental), and Sorel contributions, which align with quarterly growth patterns (E25-E28).

attrs.final_verdict: explanation does not fit the numbers

attrs.reason: Management attributes revenue growth to Columbia brand, prAna acquisition (~$56M incremental), Sorel brand, and a channel mix shift to direct-to-consumer. The evidence pack provides total revenue (E12), quarterly revenue (E25-E28), gross margin expansion (E37), and MD&A statements (E36, E37, E38) that quantify the prAna incremental ($56M) and note product category growth. However, brand-level (Columbia, Sorel) and channel-level (DTC vs wholesale) revenue breakdowns are not present as reported numbers (XBRL facts or MD&A figures). The only quantified driver is the prAna figure, which is itself a management claim. The other named drivers are not visible in the numbers, so the explanation rests largely on management's word.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The 10.7% revenue growth ($225.6M) is accounted for by the prAna acquisition contributing approximately $56M of incremental sales in the first five months of 2015 (E36), strong Columbia and Sorel brand growth (E36), and a favorable channel mix shift toward higher-margin direct-to-consumer sales (E37, E38), which is corroborated by gross margin expansion from 45.5% to 46.1% (E37).

attrs.reason: Gross margin expansion of 60 bps (45.5% → 46.1%) is attributed to a channel mix shift toward higher-margin direct-to-consumer (DTC) sales and away from lower-margin international distributors. However, the evidence pack contains no reported numbers for revenue by channel (DTC, wholesale, distributor) to verify the mix shift or its magnitude. The annual DSO improvement (60→58 days, E23) is consistent but not direct evidence of the claimed driver.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: Gross margin expansion of 60 basis points (45.5% to 46.1%) is driven by a favorable channel mix shift toward higher-margin direct-to-consumer sales and away from lower-margin international distributor sales, consistent with the stable annual DSO (60 to 58 days) despite quarterly fluctuations.
